summary: Your own AI from the first minute: installing asks nothing, and FBRX opens straight into a chat with an AI that runs on your computer.
notes: Install FBRX OS asks nothing: it builds the AI into FBRX and downloads a small AI model (about 1 GB) while it works, so the first thing you see is a chat with your own AI.
Installed with the Setup file or the Mac download? FBRX gets its AI the first time it opens and shows the progress in the chat, with Try again if the internet drops.
The first start is one screen: what Fabrix should call you, then Start chatting. Restoring a backup and joining your organization are a click away there.
Essentials is now your AI on its own: the chat, its memory and voice, AI models and Settings. Storage, FBRX Shield, notes, tasks and the rest are in Standard, one switch away in Settings → Edition.
AI models is in Essentials and Standard.
The easter eggs now come with every edition, once you find the key.
Already using FBRX without an AI? AI models has the small starter model, one click.
On a Mac: the ready-made .dmg follows soon. Until then, Install FBRX OS.command in FBRX-OS.zip installs or updates to 1.9.9.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.0: image backups that prove they work, and roles you change from the console.
notes: The time role (FBRX Time): backs up the server's virtual machines on a schedule, keeps the images computers send it, and checks every image by starting it as a throwaway virtual machine with no network. Restores an image as a new virtual machine.
Roles: switch roles on or off from the console's Roles page, or with sudo fbrx-server roles.
From 0.1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit. A 0.1.0 server updates by hand once (see SERVER.md).
FBRX Command keeps a computer's connection open longer between requests, so a busy computer no longer sees the odd failed request (enrolling, check-ins).
